newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Dec 13 - Our final estimate on CPO production in November shows a marginal downward revision of 2,000 tonnes to 762,000 tonnes. This represents a drop of nearly 122,000 tonnes or 14 percent from the previous month. The performance of major producers/millers mostly ranged from down 10-18 percent. Production in Peninsular Malaysia is estimated to have dropped by slightly more than 13 percent. The seasonel downtrend also started in East Malaysia where production fell an estimated 15 percent or 35,000 tonnes.

Production declines so far this month ranged from 10-20 percent. The bigger declines were reported by producers whose harvesting operating were adversely affected by the current rainy spell. There were however no reports of any serious floods. The estimate on end-November stocks of palm oil is also lowered by 5,000 tonnes to 960,000 tonnes as against 953,000 tonnes a month earlier. Although stocks of CPO are estimated to have remained at the month ago level, stocks were lower in East Malaysia but rose in Peninsular Malaysia with most refiners comfortably stocked up because of price discount for the current month versus deferreds.

Stocks of PK/PKO meanwhile declined an estimated 8,000 tonnes to around 175,000 tonnes, oil basis. This reflected lower output of PK coupled with strong demand for PKO. After dropping as much as 23 ringgit in the first seven days of this month with February CPO futures settling at 1184 ringgit on December 10, the market had recovered 36-27 ringgit in the last two days. The spot December contract recovered the most to settle at 1,212 ringgit as against 1,210 ringgit for February following active shortcovering activities prompted by lack of physicals traders.

An intensification of the wet weather coupled with a pickup in export sales also lent support. Last but no least, domestic price of CPO and RBD OLN in Indonesia continued to remain above price levels in Malaysia. This resulted in less competition for Malaysian palm oil in the export market. Continuing high world market price for CNO have also benefited palm oil in both Malaysia and Indonesia as consumers switched to lower-priced RBD OLN. Latest USDA supply-domestic figures for 1996-1997 left SB production estimate unchange at 2,403 million bushels but lowered projection on SB ending stocks by 30 million bushels to 180 million bushels.

SBO stocks were reduced 115 million lbs to 2,140 million lbs on account of a cut in output due to a drop in the OER. Current pace of US exports sales of SB + products also continued at a strong pace reflecting robust purchases by China.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
